Pins are clusters like the campus map: a pin holds places. legs: [pinA, pinB, minutes on foot] between pin centres; in: minutes from a place to its pin's centre (a move inside one pin takes in(a) + in(b), at least 5). locked: the castle pin, hidden on the map and closed past the White Line except to the Kingdom Competition winners (royal reception). hidden: shown on the map only once visited (the Rookery). out: outdoors (weather). generic aliases need Avalon named in the Location or {{user}} already in Avalon. rates: per hour in the city, in percent. 1.84.0 (owner-approved planning/DRAFT_kingdom_competition.md): kc 1 / kc 2 marks the Kingdom Competition's round-one field (the Kingsmeadow, beyond the Great Gate) and round-two dungeon (the Undercroft, under the arena): open only to the teams still in, during that round (engine stepKingdom); brief: the index's few words for a place the lore generator has no brief for.

places.name: Eldrasil Castle
places.desc: The royal seat at the top of the hill, white towers higher than anything in the city but the Great Spire, deep blue and gold banners on every tower. The King lives and rules here. The royal road climbs to it from Crown Square through the Noble Ring.

places.name: Noble Ring
places.desc: The townhouses of the noble families on the terraces around the castle: gardens behind white walls, quiet streets, private guards at the gates. The Noble Houses' Liaison keeps its offices here.

places.name: Crown Square
places.desc: The great square at the foot of the castle hill, where Crown Avenue ends and every avenue of the city meets the Crown Ring. The parade finishes here on Crowning Day, the Royal Mages at its head, and the King speaks from the dais on the White Line; the Herald Spires carry the speech to the whole city. Fountains, a column to the War of Independence, food stalls on holidays.
places.vibe: The heart of the kingdom, in white stone and blue banners.

places.name: Grand Cathedral
places.desc: The house of Asmoday for the whole kingdom, white and immense, its nave open to anyone. Every cathedral in Eldrasil, Halvard's included, answers to it. Sermons on the hour on holy days; the registry of oaths sworn in the capital is kept in its undercroft.

places.name: The Chancery
places.desc: The crown's offices in one long white building around a courtyard: ministries, courts, the Royal Inspectorate's headquarters, the royal archive. Open to the public in its front halls for petitions; nobody goes in for fun.

places.name: High Dovecote
places.desc: The headquarters of the Doves, a white tower with a walled courtyard of grey uniforms. The public may stand at its gate; nobody walks in. Mages in academy uniform are noticed here.

places.name: Royal Bank
places.desc: The kingdom's bank behind a long white colonnade, where Halvard's Banking House sends its ledgers. Coin changed, accounts opened, loans signed. The Arslan World Bank keeps an office in the same street.

places.name: Skyport
places.desc: Airship masts and a paved landing field just outside the Great Gate, the main gate in the south wall, with the customs hall and the passenger halls inside it. Every academy trip lands and musters here.
places.vibe: Masts, balloon envelopes and the whole city rising in front of you.

places.name: Gilded Arcade
places.desc: Two glass-roofed shopping arcades either side of Crown Avenue, just inside the Great Gate. Ardenne's flagship store, the original Merryhew's, Firetooth's own sweet shop, cafés, tailors and jewellers. Expensive, polished, and the first thing most visitors see.

places.name: Lantern Market
places.desc: Avalon's biggest market: covered streets and a glass market hall hung with paper lanterns that are lit at dusk. Food from every province, cheap clothes, charms, imported goods, street performers, pickpockets.
places.vibe: Lanterns, awnings, shouting, frying, and your purse to watch.

places.name: Spellwright Row
places.desc: The street of the magic trades. Staff and wand makers, component sellers, enchanters, rune engravers, spellbook dealers, a shop for duelling gear. Stock the academy Mall never carries, at capital prices; every shop holds a Doves licence on the wall.

places.name: Old Town
places.desc: The one grey quarter: narrow crooked lanes of grey stone from before independence, taverns, old bookshops, fortune tellers, the cheapest food in the city. Easy to get lost in. Everyone in Avalon has heard that somewhere in Old Town a door leads down into the Rookery, the city's underbelly; nobody respectable admits to knowing which one.
places.vibe: Grey stone, crooked lanes, and doors nobody talks about.

places.name: The Rookery
places.desc: Avalon's underbelly, a warren of old cellars, cisterns and smugglers' tunnels beneath Old Town, older than the white city above it. Its people call themselves rooks, a joke at the Doves' expense. A black market (stolen goods, contraband, unlicensed components, forged papers), gambling dens, a fighting pit where unlawful duels are fought for coin, and brokers who sell information to anyone. Lantern-lit, crowded, polite in its own way: rooks do not rob guests who behave, and they never forget a face that brings the Watch. Students are forbidden to go there.

places.name: Skywheel Fair
places.desc: A permanent fairground on the old parade ground at the edge of Old Town. Its giant wheel, turned by magitech, gives the second-best view in Avalon after the Great Spire and is the city's favourite place for a date; around it, games of skill with prizes, sweet stalls, a carousel and fortune booths. Busiest on holidays and at dusk, when the wheel lights up.
places.vibe: Music, sugar, and the city tilting below the wheel.

places.name: The Great Spire
places.desc: The tallest of the seven Herald Spires and the oldest, a slender white tower inside the north wall with a public viewing gallery near the top (a small fee in coin; a long stair or the lift). From the gallery the whole white city lies in its rings.

places.name: Garden of Avalon
places.desc: The city's great public garden: lawns, flower terraces, a long reflecting pool and shaded walks, busiest on holidays. At its centre stands the Archmage, the largest statue in Eldrasil: a figure in white stone, taller than the trees, staff raised over four seals cut into the ground around the plinth. The face under the hood is smooth and the plinth carries no name, because no record keeps either; visitors argue about it.
places.vibe: Flowers, still water, and a hero with no face.

places.name: Grand Theatre
places.desc: The domed white opera house of the capital beside the garden. Opera, plays and concerts; on Crowning Day a cheap afternoon matinee for the holiday crowd.

places.name: Royal Arena
places.desc: The open-air stadium of the kingdom, white stone tiers round a sand floor, warded for magic duels; the Kingdom Competition is fought here. Great scrying crystals hang above the tiers and show the crowd the rounds fought away from the sand; beneath the sand lies the Undercroft. On other days: tournaments, races, shows.
places.vibe: Ten thousand seats and the sand where reputations are made.

places.name: Whitestone Hotel
places.desc: The grand hotel beside the arena where the four academies' Kingdom Competition teams stay. Doormen, a lobby that never sleeps, a courtyard fountain, and a dining room where rival teams pretend not to look at each other.

places.name: Judges' Pavilion
places.brief: the panel's white pavilion, start and sunset hand-in
places.desc: A white pavilion with the royal blue and gold on its poles where the Kingsmeadow road meets the grass: the competition panel's table, the four academies' banners, a healer's tent beside it. Round one starts here at dawn, and here at sunset the judges take one Kingsbloom from each team.

places.name: Long Meadow
places.brief: open grass to the horizon, nowhere to hide
places.desc: Waist-high grass rolling away from the pavilion in long waves, a few lone oaks, larks going up wherever someone walks. Everything moving out here can be seen from far off.

places.name: Willow Brook
places.brief: a willow-lined stream with stepping stones
places.desc: A clear stream winding under old willows, stepping stones at the shallows and a footbridge of three planks; the banks are soft and keep footprints.

places.name: Old Orchard
places.brief: a crown orchard gone half wild
places.desc: Rows of old apple and pear trees from a royal estate long gone, gone half wild, windfalls in the grass and a collapsed press house at the end of the rows.

places.name: Bramble Hollow
places.desc: A sunken hollow choked with bramble and blackthorn, narrow tracks through it that badgers made and nobody else can walk upright; the best place in the Kingsmeadow to wait unseen.

places.name: Standing Stones
places.brief: an old stone ring on a rise
places.desc: A ring of eleven grey standing stones on a low rise, older than the kingdom; the panel's wards hum faintly between them, and the grass inside the ring is short and dry.

places.name: Reed Marsh
places.brief: reed beds and black water, wet to the knee
places.desc: Reed beds taller than a person around pools of black water, duckboards laid by the panel along one line only; off them, it is wet to the knee and loud with every step.

places.name: Beacon Hill
places.brief: the high point, a cold beacon and a view
places.desc: The highest ground in the Kingsmeadow, crowned by an old beacon basket on a stone post; from the top the whole field shows, and so does whoever stands on it.

places.name: Undercroft Gates
places.brief: three iron gates under the arena, one per team
places.desc: A long vaulted hall at the foot of the stairs under the arena, warded lamps in brackets, and three iron gates into the Undercroft, one for each team still in. A board of ten sigils by the stairs lights a room's sigil in the colour of the team that holds it.

places.name: Undercroft Room 1
places.desc: The Pillar Hall: a low hall of squat pillars close enough to touch, lamplight broken into stripes between them.

places.name: Undercroft Room 2
places.desc: The Cistern: a flooded vault with a stone walkway round its edge and still black water in the middle.

places.name: Undercroft Room 3
places.desc: The old Armoury: empty weapon racks on every wall, a broken portcullis half down across the far arch.

places.name: Undercroft Room 4
places.desc: The sunken Chapel: three steps down to a stone floor, a plain altar, niches in the walls where candles once stood.

places.name: Undercroft Room 5
places.desc: The Gallery: a narrow balcony room above a drop into darkness, a rail on one side, the wards glowing along the edge.

places.name: Undercroft Room 6
places.desc: The Kennels: a row of barred stalls where the arena's beasts were kept between shows, straw still on the floor.

places.name: Undercroft Room 7
places.desc: The Furnace room: a great cold furnace with an iron door, flues climbing into the dark, soot on every surface.

places.name: Undercroft Room 8
places.desc: The Vault: a round room behind a door a hand thick, shelves cut into the stone, the air dry and still.

places.name: Undercroft Room 9
places.desc: The Pit: a sand-floored fighting pit older than the arena above it, tiers of rough stone around it where a few hundred once watched.

places.name: Undercroft Room 10
places.desc: The Deep Hall: the lowest and largest room, a vault so high the lamps do not reach its roof, and every sound comes back twice.
